headlines.title: How Much Verizon Stock Does a 65-Year-Old Need to Collect $2,000 a Month in Dividends?
headlines.summary: A $24,000 dividend paycheck sounds simple until you see what one telecom giant demands up front, how the checks actually arrive, and what a single board decision could do to your monthly budget.

headlines.title: Inside Dan Schulman’s war on the old Verizon
headlines.summary: The former PayPal CEO left a Montana ranch to shake up one of America’s most profitable companies.

headlines.title: An $850,000 Portfolio in Verizon, Enterprise Products and UPS Pays $51,000 a Year in Dividends. Here’s What Happens if One Cuts
headlines.summary: Key TakeawaysAn $850,000 portfolio split evenly across Verizon, Enterprise Products Partners and UPS pays about $51,200 a year in dividends, or about $4,270 a month. Verizon and Enterprise Products have plenty of cash behind their payouts, from businesses that are still growing.

headlines.title: Verizon Communications (VZ) Lands Thames Freeport 5G Role As Takeover Talk Returns
headlines.summary: Verizon Communications (NYSE:VZ) has been selected to deploy a major private 5G platform at Thames Freeport in Europe. The Thames Freeport project is described as one of Europe's largest private 5G networks for logistics and manufacturing operations. Analysts are discussing the possibility that SpaceX could pursue a takeover of a large US wireless operator, with Verizon mentioned among potential targets.

headlines.title: Democrats Take Congress: 4 Dividend Stocks From Oil to Telecom Worth Buying
headlines.summary: With Democrats holding Congress and a Republican in the White House, gridlock looms for Washington. Four dividend payers span oil, defense, real estate, and telecom, and each one's cash flow looks built to shrug off the stalemate. One is vulnerable to a very different threat.

description: Verizon Communications Inc., through its subsidiaries, engages in the provision of communications, technology, information, and streaming products and services to consumers, businesses, and governmental entities worldwide. It operates in two segments, Verizon Consumer Group (Consumer) and Verizon Business Group (Business). The Consumer segment provides wireless services across the wireless networks in the United States under the Verizon and TracFone brands and through wholesale and other arrangements; and fixed wireless access (FWA) broadband through its wireless networks, as well as related equipment and devices, such as smartphones, tablets, smartwatches, and other wireless-enabled connected devices. The segment also offers wireline services in the Mid-Atlantic and Northeastern United States, as well as Washington D.C. through its fiber-optic network, Verizon Fios product portfolio, and a copper-based network. The Business segment provides wireless and wireline communications services and products, including FWA and wireline broadband, advanced communication services, corporate networking, security and managed network, local and long-distance voice, and network access services to deliver various IoT services and products to businesses, government customers, and wireless and wireline carriers in the United States and internationally. The company distributes its products and services through direct channels, company-operated stores, digital and omnichannel platforms, indirect agents, business solution resellers, and national retailers. The company was formerly known as Bell Atlantic Corporation and changed its name to Verizon Communications Inc. in June 2000. Verizon Communications Inc. was incorporated in 1983 and is headquartered in New York, New York.
